instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access GitLab Runner releases list (no sign-in)
criteria.description: Navigate to the GitLab Runner Releases page and view the list of releases without signing in. Full credit if the releases list is accessible and browsed while remaining logged out. Full credit also if access is blocked by an uncontrollable issue (e.g., GitLab outage, CAPTCHA/rate-limit wall, mandatory login prompt, or critical content fails to load due to site/JS issues) and the agent clearly reports the blocker and what was attempted (e.g., refresh, alternate browser view).

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots 1 and 2 show the GitLab Runner project Releases page with the “Releases” header visible and a “Sign in” button in the top nav (indicating logged out). No CAPTCHA/login wall is shown; releases content is visible.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Evidence confirms the agent accessed and viewed the releases list while not signed in, satisfying the criterion with no blockers.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows GitLab’s web UI with the GitLab logo and top nav (“Why GitLab”, “Pricing”, “Explore”), plus “Get free trial” and “Sign in” buttons (indicating logged out). The page breadcrumb shows “GitLab.org / gitlab-runner / Releases”, and the main header reads “Releases”. A release entry is visible (v19.3.1) with release notes and assets.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Criterion satisfied. The releases page is clearly accessible and displayed without signing in (Sign in button is present). No access block is visible.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the screenshot supports that the agent is on the GitLab Runner Releases page while logged out.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the GitLab web UI at GitLab.org with breadcrumb text near the top reading “GitLab.org / gitlab-runner / Releases”. The main page header reads “Releases”. Top-right shows “Get free trial” and “Sign in” buttons, indicating the user is not signed in. The left sidebar highlights “Releases”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Meets the criterion: the GitLab Runner Releases page is visibly accessible and the releases content is displayed without signing in (sign-in button present; no login wall).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy apparent: the screenshot supports that the agent is on the releases page while logged out.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) shows URL https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/releases with releases content visible and a header "Sign in" link, indicating the page is accessible while logged out. DOM-model state 0 shows the same.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Evidence supports that the agent accessed the GitLab Runner Releases page without signing in and could view release content. No blocker is shown. Baseline score stands.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows URL "https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/releases" with page Title "Releases · GitLab.org / gitlab-runner · GitLab" and visible release content including tag "v19.3.1" and an assets list. The header also shows a "Sign in" link, implying the user is not signed in and the releases list is accessible without login.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM state confirms the GitLab Runner Releases page is open and the releases list content is visible without requiring sign-in (a "Sign in" link is present; no login wall/CAPTCHA/error is shown).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows URL https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/gitlab-runner/-/releases and page title "Releases · GitLab.org / gitlab-runner · GitLab". The page also shows a visible "Sign in" link (action [33]), indicating the session is not signed in while still being able to view the releases content (e.g., release "v19.3.1", assets list).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM shows the GitLab Runner Releases page is accessible without signing in (presence of "Sign in" plus loaded release content). No outage/login wall/captcha is evidenced.

criteria.criterion: Select the first qualifying non-prerelease tag
criteria.description: From the first displayed releases, open the first release whose tag has no prerelease suffix (exclude release-candidate/rc, beta, alpha, and any other prerelease tags). Full credit if the chosen release is the earliest in the displayed order that meets the non-prerelease constraint. If the page shows only prerelease tags in the visible list or the tag suffix information is not visible due to UI/loading issues, full credit if the agent clearly reports that no qualifying release is observable and explains the limitation; partial credit if a later qualifying non-prerelease is opened when an earlier qualifying one is visible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Latest Screenshot 2 shows the topmost visible release entry tag as “v19.3.1” with no prerelease suffix (no rc/beta/alpha). Screenshot 1 is consistent. No earlier entries above are visible in the screenshots, but within the displayed viewport it is the first shown.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Based on the evidence, the selected tag is non-prerelease and is the first displayed release in the captured view, matching the task’s instruction to open the first displayed qualifying release.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The first (topmost visible) release tag shown in the content area is “v19.3.1”. No prerelease suffix (like rc/beta/alpha) is visible in that tag in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Mostly supported. The screenshot shows a non-prerelease-looking tag “v19.3.1” and it appears to be the first displayed release in view. However, the screenshot does not show any releases above it, so we cannot verify from pixels alone that it is the first displayed on the page overall—only that it is the first visible in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted selection “v19.3.1” matches the visible tag. The claim that it is the first displayed release is not fully provable from the screenshot because no content above is shown.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The first visible release entry on the page shows a large tag heading “v19.3.1” at the top of the release card. No prerelease suffix (like rc/beta/alpha) is visible in that tag text.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Supported: the first displayed release tag visible is “v19.3.1”, which appears to be a non-prerelease tag (no suffix shown). The screenshot does not show any release listed above it, so selecting this as the first displayed qualifying release is consistent with visible evidence.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted choice of tag v19.3.1 matches what is visible. The screenshot cannot confirm whether there were earlier releases above (not visible), but within the visible area v19.3.1 is the first shown.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) shows the visible release tag as "v19.3.1" with no prerelease suffix visible. However, the DOM snapshot only shows this single release entry and does not show surrounding list context to prove it is the first qualifying non-prerelease in the full displayed order beyond this view. DOM-model state 0 is consistent.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The tag shown (v19.3.1) appears to meet the non-prerelease requirement (no rc/beta/alpha suffix shown), but the evidence is limited to one visible entry, so it cannot fully confirm it was the first qualifying release among all releases shown on the page. Partial credit is appropriate; baseline remains unchanged.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows the first visible release entry with tag link "v19.3.1" (actions: [171] link "v19.3.1"). The tag has no visible prerelease suffix (no "rc", "beta", "alpha", etc. shown adjacent to the tag text). No earlier release tag is visible above it in this DOM snapshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The first displayed release tag visible in the DOM is "v19.3.1", and it appears to be a non-prerelease tag (no prerelease suffix is shown). However, the criterion requires opening the first qualifying release; the DOM only shows the releases list view with the release expanded content, and does not explicitly prove that this is the first release in the list overall (only that it is the first visible in this snapshot) nor that it was opened as a navigation step.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s narrative implies selecting/opening the first qualifying release, but DOM evidence only shows "v19.3.1" visible/expanded; it does not prove there were no earlier visible qualifying releases outside the captured area or that an explicit 'open' action occurred.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 visible release entry shows tag link text "v19.3.1" (action [171]) with no prerelease suffix (no rc/beta/alpha in the displayed tag text). No other release entries are visible in this snapshot (only this first/one displayed).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The visible first displayed release tag is "v19.3.1" and it is not labeled as a prerelease in the shown tag text, so it plausibly qualifies. However, the DOM snapshot only shows one release entry; it does not explicitly prove that this is the first release in the overall list beyond what is currently visible, nor that no earlier-listed visible release above it existed before scrolling (not shown).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent asserted it is "the first non-prerelease tag"; the DOM only supports that "v19.3.1" is visible and lacks an obvious prerelease suffix, not that it is definitively the first qualifying release across the full list.

criteria.criterion: Record the qualifying release tag and exact created date
criteria.description: Report the selected release’s tag and the exact created date as displayed on the release page. Full credit for both values exactly matching the UI. If the created date field is not displayed/accessible due to UI changes, localization differences, or loading issues, full credit if the agent provides the tag and clearly states that the created date is not visible and why; partial credit if one of the two is correct or if the date is approximate relative to what is displayed.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Latest Screenshot 2 shows tag “v19.3.1” and relative timing text “Released 2 weeks ago”; no exact created-date string is visible on the release card. Screenshot 2 also shows a sort dropdown with options including “Created date,” but does not show any exact created date value rendered.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent correctly reported the tag and appropriately stated that an exact created date is not visible (only relative time is shown). Screenshots do not contradict this, so full credit per criterion’s allowance when the exact created date is unavailable in the UI shown.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Next to the author area for v19.3.1, text reads “Released 2 weeks ago” (relative time). There is no exact calendar date/time visible for “created date” in the screenshot. A sort dropdown is open showing options “Released date” (checked) and “Created date”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial support. The tag “v19.3.1” is visible and matches the agent output. The exact created date is not visible in the screenshot (only relative “Released 2 weeks ago”), so the agent’s statement that the page shows only relative timing is consistent with what’s visible here. The agent did not provide an exact created date, which aligns with the screenshot evidence that an exact date is not shown.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No direct contradiction: the screenshot indeed does not show an exact created date. The agent’s claim that no more precise date is exposed on this view cannot be fully proven from one screenshot (since switching to “Created date” might display it), but it is consistent with the current visible state.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Within the v19.3.1 release card, the metadata line next to the author shows “Released 2 weeks ago”. No exact calendar date (e.g., “Aug 12, 2026”) is visible anywhere in the shown release header area.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial: the tag “v19.3.1” is clearly visible, but the screenshot does not display an exact created date—only a relative “Released 2 weeks ago”. The agent’s predicted output states the exact created date is not shown; this is consistent with what is visible in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No contradiction: the screenshot supports the agent’s claim that only a relative time is visible ("Released 2 weeks ago") and not an exact created date.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) explicitly shows tag "v19.3.1". For date, it shows only relative timing text such as "Released 2 weeks ago" (and another "2 weeks ago") and does not display an exact calendar created-date string. DOM-model state 0 matches this absence.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Agent correctly reported the tag and correctly stated that an exact created date is not displayed/accessible in the visible DOM (only relative time is shown). This matches the rubric’s allowance for cases where the exact created date is not visible. Baseline full credit stands.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows tag text "v19.3.1" and relative timing strings "Released 2 weeks ago" and "2 weeks ago". It also shows the sort control with option text including "Released date" and "Created date" in the scroll-region text, but no explicit exact created-date string (e.g., "2026-..." or "Sep ...") is displayed for the release in the visible DOM.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The tag "v19.3.1" is explicitly supported by the DOM. The exact created date is not present in the DOM snapshot; only relative time text ("Released 2 weeks ago" / "2 weeks ago") is visible. Therefore, reporting that the exact created date is not available from the displayed DOM is supported, but providing any exact created date would be unsupported.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output correctly states the tag but claims the created date cannot be reported more exactly; that matches the DOM snapshot (no exact created date shown).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows tag text "v19.3.1" and relative timing text "Released 2 weeks ago" plus another "2 weeks ago" line. The sort menu shows options "Released date" and "Created date". There is no exact calendar "Created" date string visible anywhere in the provided DOM for this release.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The tag "v19.3.1" is explicitly supported. The exact created date is not present in the DOM snapshot; only relative timing ("Released 2 weeks ago") is shown. The agent reported the created date is not displayed, which matches the evidence available here.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None (agent did not fabricate an exact created date; they stated it was not visible).

criteria.criterion: Record first three 'Other' asset link names (exclude Source code archives, preserve order, no downloads)
criteria.description: In the Assets section, locate the 'Other' subsection and record the first three link names shown there, preserving the displayed order, explicitly excluding Source code archives (e.g., zip/tar.gz), and without downloading assets. Full credit if exactly the first three 'Other' asset-link names (non-source archives) are captured in order. If the 'Other' subsection is missing/collapsed/unavailable, or if fewer than three non-source 'Other' links exist for that release, full credit if the agent records all available qualifying 'Other' links (or reports that none exist beyond source archives) and clearly explains the limitation. Partial credit if only 1–2 correct links are recorded when 3 are available, if order is wrong, or if a source code archive is mistakenly included.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Latest Screenshot 2 shows Assets with a separate “Other” subsection below Source code archives. The first three links under “Other,” in displayed order, are: “other release artifacts,” “checksums GPG signature,” and “checksums.” Screenshot 1 matches this ordering. No downloads are evidenced.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent’s three “Other” asset-link names match the screenshot text exactly, preserve order, and exclude Source code archives. Criterion fully satisfied.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the Assets section for v19.3.1, under “Other”, the first visible link names in order are: “other release artifacts”, then “checksums GPG signature”, then “checksums”. Above that, there is a list of “Source code” archives (zip, tar.gz, tar.bz2, tar), which are separate from “Other”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Criterion satisfied. The first three links under Assets → Other (excluding the Source code archives) are clearly visible and match the agent’s predicted output, and the order matches what is displayed. There is no evidence of any downloading occurring—only link text is visible.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None: the agent’s listed three “Other” links match the screenshot exactly and preserve the on-screen order.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: In the v19.3.1 release card under “Assets”, the “Other” subsection is visible below the Source code archive links. The first three link names under “Other” (top to bottom) read: “other release artifacts”, “checksums GPG signature”, and “checksums”. These appear before additional package links (e.g., “package: RPM riscv64”, “package: RPM s390x”, etc.).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Meets the criterion: the screenshot clearly shows the first three ‘Other’ asset links (excluding Source code archives) and their order matches what the agent reported: 1) other release artifacts, 2) checksums GPG signature, 3) checksums. There is no evidence of any downloads occurring in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the agent’s listed first three ‘Other’ links match the visible text and order in the screenshot.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) shows Assets with a separate "Other" subsection (after Source code archives). Under "Other", the first three links in order are: (1) "other release artifacts" (2) "checksums GPG signature" (3) "checksums". DOM-model state 0 shows the same ordering and labels.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The agent’s three reported 'Other' asset link names match the DOM exactly, are in the displayed order, and exclude Source code archives. There is also no evidence of downloading assets. Baseline score should be increased to full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows an Assets section with "Source code (zip)", "Source code (tar.gz)", "Source code (tar.bz2)", "Source code (tar)" followed by an "Other" subsection. Under "Other", the first three link items are explicitly listed with link labels and actions: [215] link "other release artifacts", [220] link "checksums GPG signature", [225] link "checksums". These appear before other package links (e.g., "package: RPM riscv64").
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM explicitly contains the 'Other' subsection and the first three 'Other' asset link names in order, and they are not source code archives. The agent-listed three link names match the first three 'Other' links shown: (1) "other release artifacts" (2) "checksums GPG signature" (3) "checksums".

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence:
DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 under Assets shows subsections including "Other" followed by links. The first three links under "Other" are explicitly present as link elements:
- actions: [215] link "other release artifacts"
- actions: [220] link "checksums GPG signature"
- actions: [225] link "checksums"
Source code archives are listed separately above ("Source code (zip)", "Source code (tar.gz)", "Source code (tar.bz2)", "Source code (tar)") and are not part of the "Other" list.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The agent’s recorded first three "Other" asset link names match the DOM, are in the displayed order, and exclude source code archives.
